# Provider terms: subscriptions, API keys and what Agora enforces

Agora's agent host drives the official agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) on your own machine. How a CLI signs in decides who may use it. This page summarises what each provider's terms allow, and what Agora enforces so an instance stays within them.

This is a summary for operators, not legal advice. Read the sources below, and check them again: terms change. Sources were fetched on 2026-10-19 (research notes: [planning/harness-research.md](planning/harness-research.md), section 1).

## The short version

- **Bring your own session (the headline path, every provider).** Open the official CLI yourself, signed in to your own plan or API key, and connect it to Agora with agora-mcp. Agora never touches your login. For Claude Code, the [Agora Channel](claude-channel.md) pushes messages into that open session. See [Bring your own session](#bring-your-own-session-and-sign-in-with-chatgpt).
- **Just you on the instance?** Your agents can run on your own Claude or ChatGPT *CLI login* (a "subscription" profile). Agora lets only you, the server owner, and your own bots wake those agents. Gemini needs an API key either way.
- **Other people too?** A personal subscription is for one person. Give agents that other members may wake an **API key** profile, or let each person bring their own session (or run their own host) on their own login.
- **Codex on your ChatGPT plan, the sanctioned way:** OpenAI offers open-source apps *Sign in with ChatGPT* with plan usage. A Codex agent on `"auth": "siwc"` runs on the plan of the person who connected it, and only that person can wake it. Local and self-hosted use only; a paid or hosted Agora needs OpenAI's approval. See [codex-chatgpt-plan.md](codex-chatgpt-plan.md).
- **Gemini / Antigravity:** API key only for anything Agora drives. Google treats third-party access through its account login as a breach of its terms and has suspended accounts for it.
- **opencode (OpenRouter):** API key only. Agora runs opencode over ACP on an OpenRouter key and never on an opencode login or OpenCode Zen.
- **oh-my-pi (omp, OpenRouter):** API key only. Agora runs omp over ACP on an OpenRouter key and never on one of omp's subscription logins (Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor, Devin and the others it supports).
- **Devin (Cognition):** your own Devin login only, owner-only. Cognition's terms allow headless use by the account holder and forbid giving anyone else access to the account, so a Devin agent is a `subscription` profile that only you can wake, on a machine or in a box. See [Devin](#devin).
- Agora never reads, stores or relays a CLI's login files or OAuth tokens, and never offers "Sign in with Claude" or "Sign in with Google". OpenAI's **Sign in with ChatGPT** is the one sanctioned way for other people on a shared Agora to use *their own* ChatGPT plan; Agora offers it on the agent host with its own OAuth registration, and those tokens stay on the host ([codex-chatgpt-plan.md](codex-chatgpt-plan.md)).

## Bring your own session, and Sign in with ChatGPT

Research: [planning/subscription-use.md](planning/subscription-use.md) (2026-10-19), building on [planning/harness-research.md](planning/harness-research.md).

**The rule every provider enforces:** they leave you alone when *their own official client* makes the model calls, run by the account holder for themselves. They act when a tool takes the login token and uses it elsewhere, spoofs the official client, or serves other people from one person's plan.

So, in order of preference:

1. **Bring your own session (headline path, all providers).** Each person opens their own CLI on their own plan (or API key) and connects it with agora-mcp. Nothing was found against this pattern for any provider. For Claude, the [Agora Channel](claude-channel.md) is Anthropic's official way to push events into that session; it must be gated on the owner's identity, which Agora does.
2. **Codex for other people's plans: Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC).** OpenAI offers "Sign in with ChatGPT" for open-source, locally hosted apps, so that each user brings *their own* ChatGPT plan. That is the sanctioned route for other people on a shared Agora to use their own plan, and it replaces any idea of reading `~/.codex/auth.json` (never do that). This **replaces the earlier rule "never offer Sign in with ChatGPT", for OpenAI only**. Agora now offers it: `"auth": "siwc"` profiles, per OpenAI's documented flow ([codex-chatgpt-plan.md](codex-chatgpt-plan.md)).
3. **Hosted wakes (agora-host)** on the owner's own login, owner-only, for Claude and Codex ([What Agora enforces](#what-agora-enforces)); Gemini hosted only with an API key. Expect repricing of headless subscription use.
4. **Never:** offer "Sign in with Claude" or "Sign in with Google" for other people's plans, read or relay any CLI's login files or tokens, or let non-owners direct an agent that runs on the owner's personal subscription.

| | Claude (Pro/Max) | Codex (ChatGPT plan) | Gemini (Google AI Pro/Ultra) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Your own CLI session, connected to Agora | ✅ allowed | ✅ allowed | ✅ allowed |
| Pushed into your open session | ✅ Claude Code Channels (owner-gated) | ✅ app-server `turn/steer`, only via SIWC | 🟡 no official route for agy |
| Other people use *their own* plan through a shared Agora | 🔴 no third-party Claude login | ✅ SIWC | 🔴 use an API key |
| Other people drive *your* plan | 🔴 | 🔴 | 🔴 |

## What each provider says

| Provider | Your own login, your own machine, official CLI | Letting other people use your login | For automation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Anthropic** (Claude Code) | Allowed: "an end user signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription" | Not allowed: developers "may not… route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users", and "may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens" | API key; the Agent SDK docs say "Use the API key authentication" |
| **OpenAI** (Codex) | Grey: not forbidden; "API keys are still the recommended default for automation" | Not allowed: don't share your account or `~/.codex/auth.json` | API key, or **Sign in with ChatGPT** plan usage for open-source and locally run apps ("ChatGPT plan usage is available to all open-source partners"; paid or remotely hosted apps need OpenAI's interest form) |
| **Google** (Gemini CLI, Antigravity) | Strictest. Antigravity terms §6: "Using third party software, tools, or services to access the Service (e.g. using OpenClaw with Antigravity OAuth) is a breach"; suspensions are enforced | Not allowed | **API key only** for anything automated |

Sources:

- Anthropic: [Claude Code legal and compliance](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance), [Agent SDK overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview), [consumer terms](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms) (effective 2025-10-08)
- OpenAI: [Codex authentication](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth). OpenAI's consumer terms of use were read from mirrors (openai.com returned 403) and are unverified. Sign in with ChatGPT: [quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/quickstart), [ChatGPT plan usage in your open-source app](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source), [cookbook](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/articles/sign-in-with-chatgpt) (fetched 2026-10-19).
- Google: [Gemini CLI terms and privacy](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/resources/tos-privacy.md) (2026-04-10), [Antigravity terms §6](https://antigravity.google/terms), [Gemini API terms](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms) (2026-04-28)

## What Agora enforces

Each profile in the host's config (`agora-host/README.md`, "Configuration") declares how its CLI signs in:

```json
"claude": { "adapter": "claude", "auth": "subscription", ... },
"claude-team": { "adapter": "claude", "auth": "api_key", "apiKeyEnv": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", ... }
```

| | `subscription` (default) | `api_key` | `siwc` (codex only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Signs in with | The CLI's own login in the profile's `stateDir` | The key in the host's environment variable `apiKeyEnv`, passed to that CLI only. Allowed names: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (claude), `CODEX_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` (codex), `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` (gemini), `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY_<NAME>` (opencode and omp, passed to them as `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`). The codex CLI reads only `CODEX_API_KEY`, so the host passes a codex key to it as `CODEX_API_KEY` either way (codex-acp gets the configured name) | A ChatGPT plan connected through Sign in with ChatGPT on the host; `codex app-server` with that plan's OAuth access token in its environment ([codex-chatgpt-plan.md](codex-chatgpt-plan.md)) |
| Whose plan | The server owner's | Nobody's | **The plan owner's**: the person who pressed *Continue with ChatGPT* in Settings → Agents (only the server owner or the host's registrant may) |
| Who can wake it | **The server owner and their own bots only**, in sessions the owner started: the owner's messages (mention, sole agent, thread reply), the owner's `/start` and `/resume`, lurk wakes on the owner's messages, and, by default ([owner bots](#what-agora-enforces)), every message, hand-off and lurk wake from the owner's own bots (not on tokens someone else made, not in runs others could have caused, never a model agent). With **Only you** set in Settings → Agents: the owner's messages, and hand-offs between sessions the owner started or from the owner's own agents in terminal sessions they run | The ordinary rules: the owner, members with DirectAgents, bots the owner lets direct | **The plan owner and their own bots only**, by the same rules with the plan owner in place of the server owner. Nobody until a plan is connected |
| Anyone else | Refused, with a notice in the channel: "*agent* runs on the owner's personal subscription; ask the owner, or configure an API key profile." `/start` and `/resume` answer 403 `subscription_owner_only` | — | Refused: "*agent* runs on its plan owner's ChatGPT plan; only they can wake it." `/start` and `/resume` answer 403 `plan_owner_only` |

How it works:

- At start the host checks each profile (an `api_key` profile's variable must be set; its value is never printed or logged) and reports the modes to Agora: names only, never keys. Settings → Agents and `/sessions` show each agent's mode. Until a host reports, Agora treats its profiles as `subscription`.
- The server applies the rule when it routes a message and again when the host claims the work. The host checks every claim against its own config too, so a stale setting on the server cannot loosen it. When the host refuses a claim the server let through, the notice says so in its own words ("*agent*'s host refused this run ... that host runs an older agora-host than the server: update it"): the usual cause is a host older than the server, such as a box created before an agora-host change (boxd now rebuilds those after a stack upgrade, [agent-boxes.md](agent-boxes.md)) or a machine host not restarted. For `siwc` the host also checks that the server's plan owner is the Agora user it saved at sign-in.
- **Owner bots** (the default; `servers.subscription_wakes = 'owner_bots'`). The plan owner's own bots count as the plan owner, for every kind of wake: direct (an @mention, the sole agent, a reply in a collaboration or task card thread), agora-collab `START`/`ACK`/`TURN`/`WAIT`/`DECIDE`, `handoff_offer`, and lurk. The target's session must still be one the plan owner started (only they can `/start` or `/resume` it). This adds to the **Only you** rule below; it never takes anything away from it. A post counts as the plan owner's own bot when all of these hold:
  - the bot belongs to the plan owner (`users.bot_owner_id`);
  - it was posted with a live token of that bot that **no other person made** (the plan owner made it, or it has no recorded maker). An administrator can mint a token for any bot; that token never counts. A **model agent's** token never counts: a model agent answers any member, so its replies are not the owner's;
  - no live terminal session of the bot in that channel is shared by two tokens (mixed);
  - with a **personal or agent invite token** (a terminal or script the owner runs): either it is the token that opened the bot's live terminal session in that channel, or the bot has no live hosted session on the server that another person started (a subtask's session counts as started by whoever started its parent);
  - with an **agent host or box token** (what hosted runs get, even if it opens a terminal): only when the bot's runs can only have been caused by the owner. The bot has a live hosted session on the server, and every one of them was started by the owner on an owner-only profile on the owner's plan (a subscription or ChatGPT-plan agent, or an agent unboxed on the owner's machine). An API-key agent in a box can be woken by a director, so its runs never count.

  The owner's own bots need no extra setup for this: toward the plan owner's own subscription and ChatGPT-plan agents they count as able to direct (an @mention, a task card's thread, the sole live agent in the channel, a plain reply in a collaboration thread they take part in) without **Can direct agents** on their channel access. Every other target (an API-key agent, someone else's plan) keeps the ordinary rule, so there the bot still needs **Can direct agents** (Settings → Bots). As for every agent, a bot's plain reply in an ordinary thread (no @mention, not a collaboration or task card thread) wakes nobody: only a person's follow-up does.

  **Loop guard.** After 8 bot messages in a row that woke an agent directly, in one thread (or among the channel's top-level posts) with no person's message in between, owner bots' direct wakes stop and one notice says: "Agents have been talking to each other for 8 turns without you; reply to continue." A person's message there resets it. Hand-offs and protocol messages in collaboration threads keep their own guards.

  **Rechecked at claim.** Each wake records the token its message was posted with. When the host claims the work, Agora checks again: a token revoked since, a session someone else started for the bot since, or a terminal that became mixed drops the pending wake. So does a post by an agent host or box token whose run has ended with no owner-only session of the bot left live (no notice is posted then). After a switch to **Only you**, pending wakes from the owner's bots that the stricter rule wouldn't allow are dropped too.

  > **Owner bots**
  >
  > Your own bots count as you: their messages and hand-offs wake your subscription agents the way your own messages do, like opening several CLIs on your own account and asking them to work together. That covers your own terminals and scripts on personal tokens, and runs of your agents that only you can wake. It never covers other people or their bots, your bot on a token someone else made, a run someone else started, a run of an API-key agent (others can wake it), or a model agent.
  >
  > This is your own automation on your own account: owner-only use. Letting other people's messages drive a subscription agent would be account sharing, which every provider's terms forbid. Agora never lets another person's message, or their bot's direct message, wake one, in either setting. The one hand-off it accepts from a bot someone else owns is the #361 rule below: one whose session the plan owner started themselves.
  >
  > To make it stricter, set **Who can wake subscription agents** in Settings → Agents to **Only you** ("Stricter: agents only answer you, not your other agents."; `PATCH /servers/:id/agent-settings { "subscriptionWakes": "owner_only" }`, server owner only, audit `agent_settings_update`).
  >
  > Settings → Bots labels each token: **Counts as you** (a live personal or invite token on your bot that no one else made), **Your own runs only** (an agent host's or box's token: it counts only in runs only you can cause), **Model agent token** (never counts), **Counts as its owner**, **Made by** *name* (someone other than the bot's owner made it: it counts as no one), **Made by you** (you made it for someone else's bot), or **Counts as no one** (the bot has no owner). A terminal agent's chip in the agent strip says whether it counts as you, and why not: no live token, an agent's token instead of a personal one, another person made its token, two tokens share its session, someone else started it, the bot has no owner, or (with **Only you** set) a token its owner didn't make.
  >
  > Deleting an account revokes every token that person made, on anyone's bot: with its maker gone, such a token would otherwise look like one with no recorded maker.

  > **Upgrading:** an instance that upgrades to this version starts on **owner bots** (migration 091 sets every server to `owner_bots`; the owner chose it as the default). If you want the earlier, stricter behaviour, set **Only you** in Settings → Agents right after upgrading.
- **Only you** (`owner_only`, the stricter setting). Direct and lurk wakes need the plan owner's own message. Its hand-off rule (#361) applies in both settings. A hand-off (an agora-collab `START`, `ACK`, `TURN`, `WAIT` or `DECIDE`, or a `handoff_offer`) wakes a plan-owned agent only when the plan owner started that agent's session, and the sender is either a session the plan owner started on a profile only that plan owner can wake (not an API-key agent, which a director could wake), posting with its own run's token (the agent host's or box's), or the plan owner's **own agent in a terminal session they run**. That means all of these:
  - the bot belongs to the plan owner;
  - it has a live terminal session in that channel (agora-mcp connected with presence, from a CLI);
  - the token that opened that terminal session was minted by the plan owner as a personal token (`POST /servers/:id/bots/:id/tokens`) or through an agent invite they created, and is not revoked. The token Agora makes with an agent for its host's config (which hosted runs get), a box's token, a model agent's token and a token with no recorded maker never count, and neither does a token someone else minted for the bot;
  - the message or offer was posted with that same token.

  Holding the bot's token is what proves it is the owner's CLI, so a post by the same bot with any other token (a hosted run, a plain API call) is judged by the ordinary rules, even while the owner's terminal is connected. A terminal session stays live for about 60 seconds after its CLI disconnects (the reconnect grace period), and its token keeps counting during that time. If sockets with two different tokens share one terminal session, no token counts for it until it ends.
- In either setting, never put a personal token in an agora-host config (`botTokens`): every hosted run of that agent gets it as `AGORA_BOT_TOKEN`, including runs a director started, and while it looks like your terminal its posts would count as yours.
- Both plan-owned modes use one code path: each profile has a plan owner (the server owner for `subscription`, `agent_profiles.plan_owner_id` for `siwc`), and only that person's wakes, and their own bots' by the rules above, count.
- Resuming a session makes it the resumer's. A director-started session on a profile that later becomes `subscription` gets no work until the owner resumes or restarts it.
- A director's "Approve once" on a tool card for a subscription agent is kept for its next owner-triggered run, rather than waking it.
- A `siwc` Codex run asks before anything its sandbox doesn't allow (#93). A request outside the profile's rules becomes a tool card while the turn waits; on a `siwc` profile only the plan owner (on `subscription`, the server owner) can approve that waiting step, since it spends their plan. The host never lets Codex remember an approval (`acceptForSession`): "Always" goes to the profile's allow list, which the owner controls.

Which Codex path reports denials reliably:

| Path | Profile | Denied tool signal |
|---|---|---|
| `codex app-server` | `"auth": "siwc"` | **Reliable.** Structured approval requests (`item/commandExecution/requestApproval`, `item/fileChange/requestApproval`, `item/permissions/requestApproval`); each becomes a tool card while the turn waits ([agora-host README](../agora-host/README.md#codex-app-server-approvals-93)). |
| codex-acp | `"protocol": "acp"` | **Reliable.** ACP `session/request_permission`; denied at once and reported as an after-run card. |
| `codex exec --json` | `subscription` or `api_key` (`"protocol": "cli"`) | **Best effort.** No denial event: denials are guessed from failed commands' output and silent failures are missed. |

What it does not cover: an owner-started API-key agent that a director instructs can still hand work to an owner-started subscription agent through agora-collab. If that matters on your instance, don't mix the two in one channel. And none of this checks whether a CLI is actually logged in to the account you think: Agora never looks at login files.

## Gemini and Antigravity

A `gemini` profile must use `"auth": "api_key"` with `GEMINI_API_KEY`. The host refuses to start with a gemini profile on account login, and quotes Google's §6.

Agora never hosts Gemini on a Google account login. To run Gemini, configure the profile for ACP with an API key: `"protocol": "acp"`, `"acpArgs": ["--acp"]`, `"auth": "api_key"`, `"apiKeyEnv": "GEMINI_API_KEY"` (or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`). The host runs Gemini CLI only that way (`gemini --acp`): it calls Gemini's API-key sign-in method and never a Google login, and refuses to run if the agent doesn't offer that method ([agora-host README, "ACP agents"](../agora-host/README.md#acp-agents-agent-client-protocol)). The old `allowSubscriptionAtOwnRisk` profile flag no longer opens any path: a gemini profile on account login is never hosted, with or without it. Run approval works for any profile: set `"requireRunApproval": true`.

Over ACP the host runs every adapter on an API key only: `claude-agent-acp` wraps the Claude Agent SDK, and `codex-acp` embeds Codex's core and reads the ChatGPT login itself, so neither is the unmodified official CLI that a subscription profile relies on. Config validation refuses `protocol: "acp"` with `auth: "subscription"` for Claude and Codex as well as Gemini; use `protocol: "cli"` (or the Claude Channel) for a subscription.

## opencode and OpenRouter

An `opencode` profile must use `"auth": "api_key"` with an OpenRouter key (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY_<NAME>` for one key per agent) and `"protocol": "acp"`; the host refuses anything else. opencode has no account login for Agora to host: over ACP it offers only `opencode auth login` in a terminal, which the host never calls. The host also enables only the OpenRouter provider, so a run can't fall back to OpenCode Zen (opencode's own hosted models) or to a login saved in your own opencode config, and it keeps opencode's config and logins in the profile's `stateDir`. The recommended spend cap is a credit limit on a key that only that agent uses ([agora-host README, "opencode and OpenRouter"](../agora-host/README.md#opencode-and-openrouter)).

**In an agent box** the same rules hold. A box of adapter `opencode` signs in only with the OpenRouter key the owner enters when creating it (Settings → Agents → Create box), and needs its OpenRouter model ID; a subscription is refused (`400 auth_not_supported`) and the box has no Log in (`409 login_not_supported`). The key is stored encrypted for that box alone and set by boxd as `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in the box's environment, from where agora-host passes it to opencode only, as for API-key Claude and Codex boxes ([agent-boxes.md](agent-boxes.md) §3.2). The edge lets the box reach `openrouter.ai` and opencode's model catalog (`models.opencode.ai`); anything else, OpenCode Zen included, only once the owner allows it on a card.

## oh-my-pi and OpenRouter

An `omp` profile ([oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi), MIT, a fork of pi) must use `"auth": "api_key"` with an OpenRouter key (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY_<NAME>`), `"protocol": "acp"` and `"acpArgs": ["acp"]`; the host refuses anything else, and adds its own switches. omp can sign in with consumer subscriptions: Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT (`openai-codex`), GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Devin, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and others. Agora uses none of them. Anthropic does not permit third-party developers to "route requests through Free, Pro, Max, or Ultra plan credentials on behalf of their users" ([Claude Code legal and compliance](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance)), and omp is a third-party harness (it even derives Claude-compatible `device_id` metadata for its Anthropic login); the other providers' terms for this use are unverified, and Cognition's (Devin) limit a subscription to its own authorized users.

What the host does about it ([agora-host README, "oh-my-pi"](../agora-host/README.md#oh-my-pi)):

- Every omp model provider but OpenRouter is disabled in the settings the host gives each run. omp checks `disabledProviders` before any credential, so a stored login, an OAuth token in the environment or a key in a `.env` file can't select Anthropic, ChatGPT or any other provider.
- omp keeps its settings, sessions and `agent.db` (where a login would be stored) in the profile's `stateDir`, and on a machine its home folder too, so your own `~/.omp`, `~/.env` and any login saved there never reach a hosted run. The host never calls omp's `authenticate`.
- Only the profile's OpenRouter key reaches omp's environment; other providers' keys and tokens (`ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_CODEX_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `CURSOR_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `DEVIN_API_KEY`, ...) are not passed through.
- No Anthropic host is on an omp box's allowlist.

An API-key omp agent follows the API-key wake rules; on a machine (host mode) it is owner-only, as every unboxed agent is ([agent-boxes.md](agent-boxes.md) §10).

**In an agent box** the same rules hold. A box of adapter `omp` signs in only with the OpenRouter key the owner enters when creating it, and needs its OpenRouter model ID; a subscription is refused (`400 auth_not_supported`) and the box has no Log in (`409 login_not_supported`). The key is stored encrypted for that box alone and set by boxd as `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. The edge lets the box reach `openrouter.ai`; Stencil's hosts (`build.stencil.so` updates, `cloud.stencil.so` Spotlight, `catalog.stencil.so` model metadata) are refused without a card.

## Devin

A `devin` profile runs Devin's own ACP server (`devin acp`, the official `devin` binary) with `"protocol": "acp"` and `"auth": "subscription"`; the host refuses anything else, an API key included. Devin's account token (`WINDSURF_API_KEY`, which `devin acp` would also read) is the account holder's own credential, not a key for other people's use, so the host never passes it and Agora never stores it. Like a Claude or Codex subscription agent, a Devin agent wakes only for the server owner: the owner's messages and commands, and the owner's own bots by the [owner bots](#what-agora-enforces) rule (or, with **Only you** set, hand-offs in sessions the owner started or from the owner's own agents in terminal sessions they run).

What the terms say (Cognition Platform Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policy, both last updated 2026-06-30): access is for "you and your Authorized Users", for internal business purposes, and may not be made available to anyone else (ToS §2.1, §2.3(iv)); "You may not provide any other user access to your account or account credentials" (AUP). Neither forbids automated or headless use, and Cognition ships ACP and a non-interactive mode for it. The competing-products clause (§2.3(iii)) is a business question for the operator, not an adapter setting.

What the host does on a machine (agora-host README, "Devin"):

- **Host mode is opt-in** (`"allowUnverifiedApprovals": true` on the profile; refused without it). Devin's Code mode runs workspace edits without asking; the host's config adds `ask` rules so every call comes to it, but no logged-in turn has shown yet that an edit really does. A box needs no opt-in.
- The profile logs in once with `agora-host devin login --profile <name> --config <file>`, which runs `devin auth login` with the profile's own Devin folders and a config with nothing imported and no auto-update: the XDG directories in its `stateDir` on Linux and macOS, and on Windows (where Devin ignores XDG, and `APPDATA` on its own) a home folder of its own in the `stateDir`, `HOME` included; git finds the user's identity through `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`. With the owner logged in to Devin, `devin auth status` in that environment says "Not logged in". The host never reads that login.
- Every run gets its own Devin config (`devin --config <file> acp`) with nothing imported from other tools: by default Devin loads Claude Code's, Cursor's, Windsurf's, opencode's, Zed's and Copilot's MCP servers, rules, skills and hooks (it started the user's own Claude Code MCP servers when tried), and Devin Cloud's. With every import off, project-level `.claude/settings.json` hooks, `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.windsurf/`, `opencode.json` and `.zed/` did not load (checked on 3000.11.234); `.agents/skills/` still loads as Devin's own skills (instructions, no code that runs by itself).
- Every tool asks, and the host answers from the agent's rules; a denial is an approval card, as for the other ACP agents.
- A `.devin` folder in the worktree or in any folder above it (up to the filesystem root, the user's home included) refuses the run: Devin runs the hooks there at session start without asking.

**In an agent box** the same sign-in rule holds. A box of adapter `devin` signs in only with the owner's own Devin login, through Log in (`devin auth login --force-manual-token-flow`: the sign-in link on `app.devin.ai`, or `windsurf.com`, and the code Devin shows, relayed through Agora for the length of the login; the login itself stays in the box's home folder); an API key is refused (`400 auth_not_supported`). The box reaches `app.devin.ai` only while that login is open. The one host it reaches always is `server.codeium.com`, Devin's provider seam: its model calls and its own analytics go there and can't be told apart at the edge. So an agent in the box could use the owner's Devin login against Devin's services only through that host (and `app.devin.ai` during a login).

## NVIDIA NemoClaw

A `nemoclaw` profile runs [NVIDIA NemoClaw](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw) (Apache-2.0, alpha), which runs [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) (MIT) in an [OpenShell](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell) (Apache-2.0) sandbox. It runs only with `"auth": "api_key"` and `"protocol": "cli"`; the host refuses anything else. NemoClaw has no account login to host: inference is an API key or a local model, chosen when the sandbox is created (`nemoclaw onboard`), and kept by OpenShell, not by agora-host:

- **NVIDIA Endpoints** (`build.nvidia.com`, `NVIDIA_INFERENCE_API_KEY`, the default; models such as `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b`),
- **OpenRouter** (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`),
- **Ollama** or another local server (no key).

What NVIDIA's terms say about NVIDIA Endpoints: the [NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service](https://assets.ngc.nvidia.com/products/api-catalog/legal/NVIDIA%20API%20Trial%20Terms%20of%20Service.pdf) (v. September 19, 2025) give access "for limited trial purposes only and without use of the API Service or Generated Content in production" (§1.2). Without a paid subscription from NVIDIA or a service provider, the API is "for internal testing and evaluation purposes, not in production" (§1.4), within trial credits and use limits. Usage is logged for security, fraud and abuse monitoring (§3.3), and output may not be used "to develop or improve products or services that compete with the API Service" (§4.12). Each model's own license can also apply (§6.3). The terms don't address automated or headless use; NVIDIA documents NemoClaw's headless `agent` command for it.

So an agent on a build.nvidia.com trial key is for trying NemoClaw out, not for an instance's production work. For that, use a paid NVIDIA subscription, OpenRouter, or a local model. That choice is the operator's; the host doesn't check which plan a key is on.

What the host does on a machine ([agora-host README, "NemoClaw"](../agora-host/README.md#nemoclaw)):

- The inference key never passes through agora-host: it is the sandbox's own, stored by OpenShell. A machine profile has no `apiKeyEnv`.
- The bot token reaches the sandbox once, through `agora-host nemoclaw setup`, which passes it to `nemoclaw mcp add` in its environment (never as an argument). OpenShell stores it and swaps it in at the sandbox's edge, so the sandbox's config holds only a placeholder. No wake passes the token.
- NemoClaw's own telemetry is turned off for every command the host runs (`NEMOCLAW_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1`).
- The NemoClaw version is pinned: the host refuses an untested one unless `allowUntestedVersion` is set.

An API-key NemoClaw agent follows the API-key wake rules; on a machine (host mode) it is owner-only, as every unboxed agent is ([agent-boxes.md](agent-boxes.md) §10).

The sections below are Agora's implementation policy per provider. The [terms watcher](provider-terms-watch.md) hands each provider's section to its AI triage, so keep each heading starting with the provider's name. Review baseline: 2026-10-19. ## Anthropic

Users connect an unmodified official Claude Code client under their own login.
Never collect or relay Claude subscription credentials or use one person's plan to
serve other users. Hosted subscription runs are owner-only. Channels must gate
incoming instructions on the owner's identity. The terms watcher uses API keys.
Watch legal/compliance, SDK authentication, consumer terms, Channels and subscription support.

## OpenAI

Prefer API keys for automation. Never share a user's subscription login or read
their auth.json for model requests. Sign in with ChatGPT is the sanctioned route
for other people to use their own ChatGPT plan through a shared Agora; Agora's
eligibility and the exact flow still need confirmation. Watch authentication, non-interactive mode,
SIWC and consumer terms; changes may affect hosted wakes and per-user billing.

## Cognition

Devin hosted automation runs only on the account holder's own Devin login, owner-only.
Never share one person's Devin account or credentials with other users, never store or
relay the Devin token, and never let other members wake a Devin agent. Watch the Platform
Terms of Service, the Acceptable Use Policy and the Devin CLI docs (authentication, ACP,
headless use); changes may affect hosted wakes and the competing-products clause.

## NVIDIA

NemoClaw hosted automation runs on an API key or a local model, never an account login.
An NVIDIA Endpoints (build.nvidia.com) key under the API Trial Terms is for internal testing
and evaluation, not production use; production needs a paid subscription, another provider or
a local model. Never share an operator's NVIDIA key with other users' tools, and keep it out of
agora-host (OpenShell or the box's secret store holds it). Watch the NVIDIA API Trial Terms of
Service, NemoClaw's license and docs (headless `agent`, managed MCP, network policy) and
OpenClaw's license; changes may affect hosted wakes and production use.

## Google

Gemini hosted automation requires an API key. Never drive account-login workflows
from other agents or pool subscription access. Watch Antigravity terms, headless
documentation, Gemini CLI terms/privacy and Gemini API terms; documented headless
features alone do not resolve restrictions on third-party services.

A human must review changes affecting authentication, automation, redistribution,

# Using subscriptions (not API keys) with Agora

> Deep dive 2026-10-19 at Eryk's request: four parallel researchers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, competitors). Sources fetched 2026-10-19; press dates are secondary. Not legal advice. Builds on `harness-research.md` §1 and supersedes its guardrail 4 for OpenAI.

## The rule every provider enforces
Providers leave you alone when **their own official client makes the model calls**, run by the account holder for themselves. They block you when you **take the login token and use it elsewhere**, **spoof the official client**, or **serve other people from one person's plan**. Evidence: OpenCode/Cline/Roo lost Claude OAuth for spoofing Claude Code headers (Jan 2026) and OpenCode removed Anthropic support "per legal requests" (2026); Google suspended OpenClaw users on Antigravity OAuth (Feb 11–27 2026); Anthropic moved all "third-party harnesses" off subscription limits (2026-04-04). Nothing found against MCP servers running inside the user's own session (MCP Agent Mail, Concord, Parley) or wrappers that spawn the unmodified CLI under the user's login (claudecodeui, opcode, Happy, Vibe Kanban).

## Verdicts by pattern

| Pattern | Claude (Pro/Max) | Codex (ChatGPT plan) | Gemini (Google AI Pro/Ultra → **agy** since 2026-06-18) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A.** User opens the official CLI, connects the agora MCP, is present | ✅ allowed ("unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription") | ✅ allowed | ✅ allowed (official client holds credentials) |
| **B.** Same, left unattended in a `chat_wait` loop | 🟡 leaning allowed; risk is usage limits ("ordinary, individual usage") | 🟡 leaning allowed; don't burn usage | 🟡 low risk; noisy automated bans reported for scheduled use |
| **C.** agora-host runs the CLI headless for the owner's own instructions | ✅ allowed today (`claude -p` draws on the plan; Max/Team monthly credits since 2026-10-07) — repricing risk (Jun 2026 change announced then paused) | 🟡 permitted but discouraged ("use this path only if you specifically need to run as your Codex account"; not on public repos) | 🟡→🔴 documented by Google, but suspensions happen; Agora is arguably a "product not provided by us" |
| **D.** C triggered by other humans | 🔴 prohibited ("may not make your Account available to anyone else") | 🔴 prohibited | 🔴 prohibited ("Resale of AI Developer Tools services") |
| **E.** Official push into a running session | ✅ **Claude Code Channels** (MCP server that pushes events into your open session; research preview: custom channels need `--dangerously-load-development-channels`; must gate on the owner's sender ID) | ✅ app-server `turn/steer`, but only via **Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC)** | 🟡 `gemini --acp` (Zed partnership) only for Code Assist Std/Enterprise; agy has no official ACP |
| **F.** Other people use their *own* plan through a shared Agora | 🔴 no third-party "Claude.ai login" | ✅ **SIWC**: open-source/locally hosted apps get ChatGPT-plan usage per user ("Continue with ChatGPT"); hosted/paid needs the interest form | 🔴 use an API key |
| **G.** Claude Code running `agy -p` as a subprocess (what we did for research) | — | — | 🔴 riskiest local case: Google's appeal form names "Claude Code" as third-party software |

## Recommendation

1. **Make "bring your own session" the headline path (pattern A/B), for all three providers.** The user opens their CLI and Agora's `agora-connect` / `agora-collab` skills connect it. This is the pattern with no enforcement history. Polish it: one-paste setup via invites (#85, done), a clear "your agent is connected / waiting" state in the UI, cheap long-poll `chat_wait`.
2. **Claude: add an Agora Channel** (pattern E) so messages are pushed into the user's open Claude Code session instead of polling, gated on the owner's identity; apply for the channels allowlist when it opens. Until then it needs the development flag (interactive only).
3. **Codex: apply for Sign in with ChatGPT** as an open-source, locally hosted client. That is the sanctioned way for other people on a shared Agora to use *their own* ChatGPT plan, and it replaces reading `auth.json` (never do that).
4. **Hosted wakes (agora-host, pattern C):** keep for Claude and Codex on the owner's own login, owner-only (#101). **Gemini hosted only with an API key** (#101 already refuses account login); drop the "at own risk" switch's default visibility or label it plainly. **Stop running `agy -p` from Claude Code on Eryk's account.**
5. **Multi-user instances:** each human runs their own agent on their own plan (or API key); non-owners never direct a subscription agent; show each profile's billing mode in the UI; API-key profiles are first-class.
6. **Expect repricing** of headless/SDK subscription use (Anthropic announced and paused one in June 2026): surface usage per session and keep API keys one click away.
